Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the MediTech Innovations Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Dr. Emily Chen, Chief Technology Officer; and Michael Patel, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. MediTech Innovations achieved record results this quarter, reflecting the strength of our diversified portfolio and our commitment to innovation.

Today, I will cover eight key aspects of our performance:
1. Inventory management and working capital optimization
2. Impact of pricing and cost management initiatives
3. FDA approvals and CE marks obtained
4. Overall performance highlights and key achievements
5. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
6. Capital equipment vs consumables mix trends
7. R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress
8. Key assumptions underlying the guidance

Jordan will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Dr. Chen will update us on our technology advancements, and Michael will discuss our market strategies. We'll then conclude with a Q&A session.

Now, let's get started with inventory management and working capital optimization.

In the medical devices sector, products like our flagship CardioFlex stents, OrthoLink joint implants, and da Vinci-inspired minimally invasive robotic systems deliver premium margins but encounter challenges such as FDA 510(k) clearance timelines, sterilization requirements, and fluctuating costs for biocompatible resins and nitinol. Our disciplined strategy protected margins amid inflation and generated $125 million in free cash flow for the first half of 2024.

Days Inventory Outstanding, or DIO, started the year at 112 days, in line with industry standards amid supply chain issues from past semiconductor shortages affecting companies like Intuitive Surgical and Stryker. By quarter-end, we reduced it to 92 days—a sequential 18% improvement and the best among peers, compared to Medtronic's 105 days and Boston Scientific's 98 days from their latest filings.

This came from multiple initiatives. We implemented an AI-powered forecasting tool within our SAP S/4HANA system, using machine learning on five years of sales data, real-time orders from top IDNs like Mayo Clinic equivalents, and factors like CMS schedules and procedure volumes. Forecast accuracy rose to 96% for items like CardioFlex stents, which are 22% of inventory value, allowing a 15% or $78 million cut in excess stock without stockout risks during high-demand periods for hip and knee replacements.

On supply chain, after last year's resin price spikes of 25% affecting peers like Zimmer Biomet, we expanded Vendor-Managed Inventory with top suppliers like DuPont for polymers and Heraeus for coatings. They hold consignment stock at our Reno and Galway sites, cutting our raw material inventory by 28% and stretching Days Payable Outstanding to 78 days from 65. We localized 40% of nitinol sourcing to Singapore and Vietnam, halving lead times to 8 weeks and dodging Red Sea disruptions that raised freight costs for others.

In the U.S., 58% of revenues, consignment with GPOs like Vizient and Premier has hospitals holding 35% of finished goods, up from 22%, dropping implant DIO by 25 days and lifting DSO to 52 days via rebates linked to OR usage. Europe, 25% of sales, navigated EU MDR delays inflating competitors' DIO; our just-in-time sterilization pilot with Steris in Limerick cut holding costs by 12% for ethylene oxide devices. In APAC, 17% of sales, China inventory turns rose 22% via a Shenzhen DC, backing 35% procedure growth in TAVR amid aging populations.

Our Cash Conversion Cycle shrank to 66 days from 92 a year ago, beating the peer median of 85 days per Deloitte. This released $210 million in working capital for redeployment into R&D for NeuroStim neuromodulation and buybacks. Gross margins grew 240 basis points to 68.2%, with obsolescence at 1.2% versus industry 2.8%.

Ahead, we're piloting blockchain traceability by Q4 for rare earths in MRI coils, targeting sub-85-day DIO by year-end amid 12% global procedure rebound per IQVIA, to gain share in the $550 billion market.

Now, let's talk about the impact of pricing and cost management initiatives.

These efforts created $285 million in added value to adjusted EBITDA, or 180 basis points of margin expansion year-over-year. Pricing drove core ASP growth of 3.2% YoY and 1.8% sequentially, the fifth straight quarter of gains despite reimbursement pressures. In structural heart like our EvoFlow TAVR platform, we gained 4.7% via value-based contracts with 12 top U.S. IDNs, linking payments to readmissions under 5%, boosting U.S. volumes 14%.

U.S., 52% of revenue, saw flat to 1% ASPs despite 2.3% Medicare cuts, thanks to 85% commercial mix and 5-7% list hikes on CRM like pacemakers and ICDs, similar to Boston Scientific's approach. EMEA, 28%, captured 5.1% from HTA approvals in Germany and UK for NeuroPulse SCS under EU MDR. Emerging markets, 20%, led with 6.8%, including 12% local ASPs in China and India for ortho implants.

Mix shift added 1.5 points, with robotic tools at 22% of segment revenue, up from 18%, ahead of Intuitive Surgical.

Cost management yielded $175 million in run-rate savings toward $650 million yearly. Gross margins rose 220 bps to 68.4%, countering 15% rises in polycarbonate and platinum-iridium. Digital twins cut scrap 18% in catheters, saving $42 million; Lean Six Sigma in Galway boosted throughput 12%. We cut suppliers to 15, hedged 70% resins, dual-sourced post-nitinol shortages.

SG&A saw R&D dip to 11.2% via AI trials, sales virtualized 65% saving $28 million. APAC margins up 310 bps to 62% via Suzhou plant; Europe stabilized COGS with energy hedges.

This supports mid-teens EPS growth, countering 4-6% reimbursement erosion and biosimilars with outcomes data showing 25% better stent patency. Pricing to add 2-3% to 2024 growth, costs to $800 million run-rate, targeting 70% gross margins for $2.2 billion pipeline including AI ablation.

Moving on to FDA approvals and CE marks obtained.

These milestones highlight our speed through regulations. We secured three 510(k)s and one PMA in Q2, totaling nine YTD—50% above last year—via our Regulatory Excellence Program cutting timelines 28% versus FDA medians.

CardioFlow XT drug-eluting stent, building on our 12% U.S. coronary share like Boston Scientific's Synergy, got 510(k) with bioresorbable sirolimus coating showing 35% faster healing in IDE trial of 1,200 patients. Q1 2025 U.S. launch eyes $250 million peak, expanding PCI TAM to $5 billion at 7% CAGR.

NeuroGuide AI ICP monitor, with Breakthrough Designation, cleared 510(k); ML on 50,000 datasets cuts false positives 42% in TBI. $80 million revenue by FY2026 in $2.8 billion market.

PrecisionOrtho robotic knee got PMA, with haptics reducing tissue damage 30%; 15,000 units Year 1 for $180 million in $12 billion TAM.

For CE marks under MDR, four Class III including CardioFlow XT and NeuroGuide via ISO 13485; PrecisionOrtho got 12-month pack extension. U.S. aids CMS NTAP; Europe opens tenders; China NMPA filings for APCI.

Our $150 million R&D—14% of revenue—uses digital twins cutting trials 22%, cybersecurity per FDA. 15 submissions 2025 including De Novo glucose sensor; 18-22% Devices growth, 68% margins.

Next, overall performance highlights and key achievements.

Q2 revenue hit $1.52 billion, +18% reported, 19% constant currency, topping consensus. Nine straight double-digit quarters; YTD $4.41 billion for high-end 16-18% full year.

Adjusted EPS $1.32, +24%, from 210 bps gross margin to 69.2% via efficiencies and heart mix. Op margins +320 bps to 28.1%, SG&A to 32%.

Cardiovascular, 42%, +22% to $638 million; NovaFlow TAVR +35% U.S. volumes, 28% share. Ortho/Spine, 31%, +16% to $472 million; Apex Cup +40% ASCs, NovaSpine AI clearance. Diagnostics, 18%, +25% to $274 million via wearables, Philips RPM $45 million. Robotics/Endoscopy +32% to $136 million.

U.S. 62% +20%; Europe 22% +14%; APAC 28% to 12%; EM 35% to 4%.

Backlog $5.2 billion +22%; six IDEs; $450 million MicroVentures M&A for DBS. 98% delivery vs. 85% peers. AI on 2 petabytes data; 45% carbon-neutral; 20 TAVR bundles.

This sets 20%+ '25 growth.

Then, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains.

SG&A at $1.28 billion, +2.1% despite 8.4% revenue growth to $4.72 billion; ratio to 27.1% from 31.2%, lowest since 2019. TTM savings $285 million.

Via 'Efficiency 2.0': Selling (62%)—sales force -7%, AI territory tools +15% productivity to $2.76 million/rep. U.S. digital detailing -22% travel +8% conversions; EMEA headcount cuts; EM -5% SG&A.

G&A (28%)—SAP 85% complete, 12% procurement savings, Manila/Hyderabad 70% shared services, RPA 40% automation.

Marketing (10%)—digital 35% budget, 4.2x ROI LinkedIn.

$500 million buybacks funded; Q3 26.8-27.3%. GenAI pilots.

Then, capital equipment vs consumables mix trends.

Consumables 74% of $5.2 billion FY revenue (+400 bps), annuity from Titan-R robotics, implants. Capital 26% +6% to $1.35 billion.

Consumables +18% to $3.85 billion; utilization +11% to 285 procs/system via AI software; ASP +4% to $1,650.

U.S. 58% consumables 78%; EMEA 24% capital-heavy NHS deal; APAC 68% China +35% base.

R&D +22% for NanoFlex; SurgiCloud +9% utilization; BioSync M&A. FY24 consumables 76-78%, 15-18% growth.

Then, R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress.

Q2 R&D $182 million, 11.2% of revenue, + double-digits YoY; YTD $542 million +14%, toward 12% FY. R&D-to-sales 22%.

17 programs, $4.2 billion NPV. Vertex scaffold IDE complete, 92% success; NeuroStim HD Breakthrough, 68% migraine reduction; Precision Knee CE Mark, 25% ROM gain.

U.S. 70% Breakthroughs; Europe MDR; APAC 18% value. Tuck-ins $120 million; Mayo partnerships. FY $750-780 million, 40% digital/sustainability.

4-5 launches/year for double-digits.

Finally, key assumptions underlying the guidance.

FY25 revenue $12.8-13.2 billion, 8-11% reported/9-12% organic; EPS $8.45-8.75, 7-11%. Mid-single procedures + mix.

CV/Heart 6-8%, TAVR 7-9%; Ortho 5-7%, Mako-like; Neuro 10-12%; Endoscopy flat-2%. U.S. 9%, Europe 7%, APAC 12%.

Gross 68-69%, +50-100 bps; inflation 2.5% offset savings. OpEx 43-44%. R&D 11-11.5% $1.45 billion AI/bioresorbables/digital. Tax 19-20%, interest $350 million, $1 billion buybacks.

No recession, upside CMS/FDA; downside strikes/FX/NMPA.

I will now turn the call over to Jordan for a review of our financial results.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex outlined comprehensively, we delivered exceptional financial performance this quarter, with revenue growth, margin expansion, and strong cash generation across the board.

Revenue totaled $1.52 billion, up 19% constant currency, driven by procedural strength and new launches. Expenses were well-controlled, with gross margins at 69.2% and operating margins at 28.1%. Profitability metrics like adjusted EPS of $1.32 reflect our efficiency. For full-year guidance, we affirm the high end of 16-18% revenue growth, with key assumptions as Alex detailed, including procedure volumes, pricing stability, and supply chain resilience. We generated robust free cash flow, supporting $500 million in share repurchases.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Chen for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Emily Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. We are excited about the progress we are making in our technology roadmap. Our latest innovation, the PrecisionOrtho robotic system, is poised to transform orthopedic procedures with haptic enhancements reducing tissue damage. We expect FDA PMA ramp-up and further CE marks in Q4.

Building on our R&D momentum, programs like Vertex bioresorbable scaffolds and NeuroStim HD are advancing rapidly, with pivotal data exceeding benchmarks and Breakthrough status accelerating paths to market. Our pipeline diversification across cardio, neuro, and ortho positions us for multiple launches.

Next, Michael with some insights on our commercial strategy.

Michael Patel:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We are focused on driving commercial excellence and expanding our global reach. Our strategic partnerships with IDNs, GPOs, and international tenders are enabling us to access new markets and customer segments, particularly in APAC and emerging ortho ASCs. Value-based contracts and digital sales tools are enhancing adoption of high-margin consumables and robotics.

Now, back to Alex for Q&A.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Michael. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: Press star then one. Our first question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. Great quarter on inventory—can you elaborate on the AI forecasting impact and sustainability into H2?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Lisa. The AI engine has been transformative, hitting 96% accuracy by integrating IDN patterns and CMS data. We've right-sized stocks effectively, and with blockchain pilots ahead, we see continued DIO compression to under 85 days, supporting cash flow even as procedures accelerate.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
On pricing initiatives, how sustainable is the ASP growth given reimbursement cuts?

Jordan Lee:
Good question, David. Our value-based bundles and premium mix in TAVR and CRM provide insulation— we've seen five quarters of gains, and outcomes data strengthens our case against GPO pressures. Expect 2-3% contribution to growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Rachel Patel:
Regarding regulatory wins like CardioFlow XT, what's the launch timeline and revenue ramp?

Michael Patel:
Thanks, Rachel. Q1 2025 U.S. launch post-510(k), with early IDN adoptions. Peak $250 million by 2028, leveraging PCI growth and our share in complex lesions. CE marks accelerate Europe/Asia.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera:
For the consumables mix shift, any risks to utilization from supply chain?

Dr. Emily Chen:
Tom, utilization hit 285 procedures per system thanks to Titan-R AI upgrades. We've dual-sourced semiconductors and diversified fabs, maintaining 98% delivery—well positioned for 8-10% gains ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver sustainable growth.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
